label: eq:weighted-oscillator-coercivity
title: Proof
body_md:
Put $R_\theta=e^{\theta\mathcal K}Re^{-\theta\mathcal K}$ on
$\mathscr F$.  The conjugated free operator is
\[
 e^{\theta\mathcal K}L_0e^{-\theta\mathcal K}X
 =c\mathcal KX+kr_+X
 -v\sum_j\bigl(e^{-2\theta}a_jXa_j^\dagger
              +e^{2\theta}a_j^\dagger Xa_j\bigr).
\]
The two gain maps are Hilbert--Schmidt adjoints.  Their common
quadratic-form estimate follows from
\begin{align*}
 2\left|\sum_j\langle X,a_jXa_j^\dagger\rangle\right|
 &=2\left|\sum_j\langle a_j^\dagger X,Xa_j^\dagger\rangle\right|\le\sum_j\bigl(\|a_j^\dagger X\|_2^2+\|Xa_j^\dagger\|_2^2\bigr)
 =\langle X,\mathcal KX\rangle+k\|X\|_2^2.
\end{align*}
Consequently
\begin{align*}
 \operatorname{Re}\langle X,e^{\theta\mathcal K}L_0e^{-\theta\mathcal K}X\rangle
 \ge{}&(c-v\cosh(2\theta))\langle X,\mathcal KX\rangle+k(r_+-v\cosh(2\theta))\|X\|_2^2.
\end{align*}
Hence, uniformly for $0\le\theta\le\theta_*$,
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\langle X,e^{\theta\mathcal K}L_0
 e^{-\theta\mathcal K}X\rangle
 \ge \kappa_*\langle X,\mathcal KX\rangle
 -kv\cosh(2\theta_*)\|X\|_2^2.
\]
For the perturbation, Cauchy--Schwarz and Young's inequality give
\begin{align*}
 |\langle X,R_\theta X\rangle|
 &\le C_R\|X\|_2\|(\mathcal K+I)^{1/2}X\|_2\\
 &\le C_R\|X\|_2\langle X,\mathcal KX\rangle^{1/2}+C_R\|X\|_2^2\\
 &\le\frac{\kappa_*}{2}\langle X,\mathcal KX\rangle
    +\left(C_R+\frac{C_R^2}{2\kappa_*}\right)\|X\|_2^2.
\end{align*}
Thus one may take
$C_*=kv\cosh(2\theta_*)+C_R+C_R^2/(2\kappa_*)$, or any larger
positive constant, to obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-oscillator-coercivity}
 \operatorname{Re}\langle X,e^{\theta\mathcal K}Le^{-\theta\mathcal K}X\rangle
 \ge \frac{\kappa_*}{2}\langle X,\mathcal KX\rangle-C_*\|X\|_2^2.
\end{equation}

We justify the evolution estimate by finite-dimensional approximation.
Let $\mathsf P_J=\mathbf1_{[0,J]}(\mathcal K)$ and let
$L_J=\mathsf P_JL\mathsf P_J$ on its finite-dimensional range.
For $X_J(t)=e^{-tL_J}\mathsf P_JX$ and
$\theta(t)=\kappa_*t/2$, set $U_J(t)=e^{\theta(t)\mathcal K}X_J(t)$.
Since $\mathsf P_J$ commutes with $\mathcal K$,
\cref{eq:weighted-oscillator-coercivity} applies to the compressed
operator with the same constants.  For $0\le t\le s_*$ it yields
\[
 \frac12\frac{\,\mathrm d}{\,\mathrm d t}\|U_J(t)\|_2^2
 =\theta'(t)\langle U_J(t),\mathcal KU_J(t)\rangle
 -\operatorname{Re}\langle U_J(t),
 e^{\theta(t)\mathcal K}L_Je^{-\theta(t)\mathcal K}U_J(t)\rangle
 \le C_*\|U_J(t)\|_2^2.
\]
Multiplying by $e^{-2C_*t}$ and integrating gives
\[
 \|U_J(t)\|_2^2\le e^{2C_*t}\|\mathsf P_JX\|_2^2
 \le e^{2C_*t}\|X\|_2^2,\qquad0\le t\le s_*.
\]
To pass to the limit, put $u=(L+I)^{-1}X$ and
$u_J=(L_J+I)^{-1}\mathsf P_JX$.
The two variational equations imply orthogonality of $u-u_J$ to
$\operatorname{Ran}\mathsf P_J$ for the inner product of the form
$\mathcal E+\|\cdot\|_2^2$.  Therefore
\[
 \|u-u_J\|_{\mathcal E}
 \le\inf_{v\in\operatorname{Ran}\mathsf P_J}\|u-v\|_{\mathcal E}
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
because the increasing ranges exhaust the form core $\mathscr F$.
Strong resolvent convergence gives
$e^{-s_*L_J}\mathsf P_JX\to e^{-s_*L}X$ in Hilbert--Schmidt norm
\cite[Theorem~III.4.8]{engel1999one}.
Write the respective matrix coefficients as $y^{(J)}_{\mathbf m\mathbf n}$
and $y_{\mathbf m\mathbf n}$.  Since $\theta(s_*)=\theta_*$, Fatou's lemma yields
\[
 \sum_{\mathbf m,\mathbf n}e^{2\theta_*(|\mathbf m|+|\mathbf n|)}
 |y_{\mathbf m\mathbf n}|^2
 \le\liminf_J\sum_{\mathbf m,\mathbf n}e^{2\theta_*(|\mathbf m|+|\mathbf n|)}
 |y^{(J)}_{\mathbf m\mathbf n}|^2
 \le e^{2C_*s_*}\|X\|_2^2.
\]
The finite left-hand side shows that the output belongs to
$D(e^{\theta_*\mathcal K})$, and its square root proves
\eqref{eq:oscillator-smoothing}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $H=H_{0,n}+W$, $\sigma=\sigma_\beta(H)$, and
$\sigma_0=\sigma_\beta(H_{0,n})$.
Choose $c_0$ so that $\widetilde H=H+c_0I\ge I$. Outside the
finite oscillator block, $\widetilde H$ agrees with $H_{0,n}+c_0I$.
On the finite block all powers of $\widetilde H$ are bounded.
Since a coordinate ladder changes the oscillator number by one,
each bare jump $A$ satisfies
\[
 \|A\widetilde H^{-1/2}\|
 +\|\widetilde H^{1/2}A\widetilde H^{-1}\|<\infty.
\]
The finite Hermite span is a common invariant core, and
$\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-b\widetilde H})<\infty$ for every $b>0$.
These bounds verify the energy and domain assumptions of
\cite[Condition~A and Proposition~2.4]{BeckerRouzeSalzmannToAppearcmp}.
The Gaussian filter satisfies the required KMS and boundedness
conditions. The construction in that paper therefore gives a
conservative KMS-symmetric sampler.
Its standard-form operator $L\ge0$ is obtained by closing the form on
$\mathscr F+\mathbb C\sqrt\sigma$.  Here the finite $H$-spectral matrices
span $\mathscr F$, since $W$ acts inside a fixed finite oscillator
block.  We will show that $\mathscr F$ alone is a form core.

\emph{Step 1: finite-energy changes of the coefficients.}
Let $L^\ell$ and $L_0^\ell$ denote the filtered jumps for $H$ and
$H_{0,n}$, respectively, with $\ell$ ranging over the $2k$ bare
ladders.  There is a finite oscillator spectral projection $Q$ such
that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:coulomb-finite-coefficients}
 L^\ell=L_0^\ell+F_\ell,\qquad F_\ell=QF_\ell Q.
\end{equation}
Choose $J_0$ with $\Pi_M\le\mathbf1_{[0,J_0]}(\mathsf N)$ and
take $Q=\mathbf1_{[0,J_0+1]}(\mathsf N)$.
For every bare coordinate ladder $A$,
\[
 (I-Q)A\Pi_M=0,\qquad \Pi_MA(I-Q)=0,
\]
because it changes total occupation by one.  On the complement of
$\Pi_M$, $H$ and $H_{0,n}$ have the same spectral decomposition.
All changed matrix elements of the filtered jump therefore have
both source and target in $Q\mathcal H_n$:
\[
 (I-Q)(L^\ell-L_0^\ell)=0,
 \qquad (L^\ell-L_0^\ell)(I-Q)=0.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:coulomb-finite-coefficients}.  Diagonalizing
$H$ inside $\Pi_M\mathcal H_n$ does not enlarge these spaces.
We enlarge $Q$ below when further ladder actions occur.

Write the state generator as
$\mathcal L(\rho)=\sum_\ell L^\ell\rho (L^\ell)^\dagger
+M_H\rho+\rho M_H^\dagger$.
We also need the finite-energy property for the drift, including
its correction Hamiltonian.  For the bare ladder $A^\ell$, let
$A^\ell_{\nu,H}$ denote its frequency component relative to $H$.
Its free frequency is $\nu_\ell\in\{-2,2\}$.  The same support argument gives, for each frequency,
\[
 A^\ell_{\nu,H}=\mathbf1_{\{\nu=\nu_\ell\}}A^\ell+G^\ell_\nu,
 \qquad G^\ell_\nu=QG^\ell_\nu Q,
\]
with only finitely many nonzero $G^\ell_\nu$.
Equation \eqref{eq:cross-frequency-generator} at $\sigma_E=\infty$ reads
\[
 M_H=-\sum_{\ell,\nu,\mu}
 \frac{\overline{\widehat f_\eta(\nu)}\widehat f_\eta(\mu)
       e^{\beta(\nu-\mu)/4}}{2\cosh(\beta(\nu-\mu)/4)}
 (A^\ell_{\nu,H})^\dagger A^\ell_{\mu,H}.
\]
Subtracting the free expression leaves the products
\begin{align*}
 (A^\ell_{\nu,H})^\dagger A^\ell_{\mu,H}
 &-\mathbf1_{\{\nu=\nu_\ell\}}\mathbf1_{\{\mu=\nu_\ell\}}
       (A^\ell)^\dagger A^\ell=\mathbf1_{\{\nu=\nu_\ell\}}(A^\ell)^\dagger G^\ell_\mu
   +\mathbf1_{\{\mu=\nu_\ell\}}(G^\ell_\nu)^\dagger A^\ell
   +(G^\ell_\nu)^\dagger G^\ell_\mu.
\end{align*}
Every term has finite-energy support: multiplication by a ladder
adds at most one shell to the support of $G^\ell_\nu$.
After enlarging $Q$ by that shell, we have
$M_H=M_0+F_0$ with $F_0=QF_0Q$.

Put $Z=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})$ and $Z_0=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H_{0,n}})$.
Since both Hamiltonians are reduced by $\Pi_M$ and agree outside it,
for every real $a$,
\[
 (I-\Pi_M)\sigma^a\sigma_0^{-a}(I-\Pi_M)
 =(Z_0/Z)^a(I-\Pi_M).
\]
Inside the block the same product is a finite invertible matrix.
Conjugating to standard form still changes only finite-energy
coefficients:
\[
 C_\ell:=\sigma^{-1/4}L^\ell\sigma^{1/4}
 =C_\ell^0+\widetilde F_\ell,\qquad
 D_H:=\sigma^{-1/4}M_H\sigma^{1/4}
 =M_0+\widetilde F_0.
\]
Here every $\widetilde F_\ell$ has finite-energy support; the
normalizing scalar cancels in each conjugation.
KMS symmetry identifies the standard-form operator with
\[
 LX=-\sum_\ell C_\ell XC_\ell^\dagger-D_HX-XD_H^\dagger.
\]
For the free operator the two rates are
$r_\pm=|\widehat f_\eta(\pm2)|^2$, so
$r_+=e^{-2\beta}r_-$ and the formula for $L_0$ above applies.
In particular, subtraction gives the explicit perturbation
\begin{align*}
 RX={}&-\sum_\ell\bigl(C_\ell^0X\widetilde F_\ell^\dagger
 +\widetilde F_\ell X(C_\ell^0)^\dagger
 +\widetilde F_\ell X\widetilde F_\ell^\dagger\bigr)
 -\widetilde F_0X-X\widetilde F_0^\dagger.
\end{align*}
The terms with two $\widetilde F$ factors and the two drift
terms have bounded coefficients.  Each cross
term contains one free ladder and one finite-energy coefficient, so
the only unbounded maps to estimate have the form
\begin{equation}\label{eq:coulomb-mixed-maps}
 X\longmapsto F X a_j^\sharp,\qquad
 X\longmapsto a_j^\sharp X F,
 \qquad F=QFQ,\qquad a_j^\sharp\in\{a_j,a_j^\dagger\}.
\end{equation}

\emph{Step 2: the weighted perturbation estimate.}
Choose $J_Q$ so that $Q\le\mathbf1_{[0,J_Q]}(\mathsf N)$.
For $F=QFQ$ and $\theta\ge0$, spectral calculus gives
\[
 \|e^{\pm\theta \mathsf N}Fe^{\mp\theta \mathsf N}\|_\infty
 \le e^{\theta J_Q}\|F\|_\infty.
\]
These factors are uniformly bounded for
$[0,\beta/4]$.  For the ladder factors one has
\[
 e^{\theta \mathsf N}a_je^{-\theta \mathsf N}=e^{-\theta}a_j,
 \qquad e^{\theta \mathsf N}a_j^\dagger e^{-\theta \mathsf N}
 =e^\theta a_j^\dagger.
\]
For the left multiplications, the ladder relations give
\[
 \|a_jX\|_2^2=\operatorname{Tr}(X^\dagger N_jX),\qquad
 \|a_j^\dagger X\|_2^2=\operatorname{Tr}(X^\dagger(N_j+I)X).
\]
Right multiplication yields the corresponding terms with $XN_j$.
Since $N_j\le \mathsf N$, each norm is at most
$\|(\mathcal K+I)^{1/2}X\|_2$, and hence
\[
 \|a_j^\sharp X\|_2+\|Xa_j^\sharp\|_2
 \le2\|(\mathcal K+I)^{1/2}X\|_2.
\]
For example, with $F_\theta=e^{\theta \mathsf N}Fe^{-\theta \mathsf N}$,
\[
 \|e^{\theta\mathcal K}(F(e^{-\theta\mathcal K}X)a_j^\sharp)\|_2
 \le e^{|\theta|}\|F_\theta\|_\infty
 \|(\mathcal K+I)^{1/2}X\|_2.
\]
Summing the finitely many terms gives
\[
 \sup_{0\le\theta\le\beta/4}
 \|e^{\theta\mathcal K}Re^{-\theta\mathcal K}X\|_2
 \le C_R\|(\mathcal K+I)^{1/2}X\|_2.
\]
At $\theta=0$, the lower and upper free estimates give
\[
 (c-v)\langle X,\mathcal KX\rangle-kv\|X\|_2^2
 \le\langle X,L_0X\rangle
 \le(c+v)\langle X,\mathcal KX\rangle+k(r_++v)\|X\|_2^2.
\]
The bound on $R$ implies, for any $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
 |\langle X,RX\rangle|
 \le\varepsilon\langle X,\mathcal KX\rangle
   +\left(C_R+\frac{C_R^2}{4\varepsilon}\right)\|X\|_2^2.
\]
Choose $\varepsilon=(c-v)/2>0$ and absorb this term into the lower
bound.  After adding a sufficiently large multiple of $\|X\|_2^2$,
there are $c_1,c_2,c_3>0$ such that
\[
 c_1\|(\mathcal K+I)^{1/2}X\|_2^2
 \le\mathcal E(X)+c_2\|X\|_2^2
 \le c_3\|(\mathcal K+I)^{1/2}X\|_2^2.
\]
Hence the closure on $\mathscr F$ has form domain
$D(\mathcal K^{1/2})$.  The Gibbs vector belongs even to
$D(\mathcal K)$: outside the finite block its diagonal coefficients
are $Z^{-1/2}e^{-\beta(k+2|\mathbf n|)/2}$, so
\[
 \|(\mathcal K+I)\sqrt\sigma\|_2^2
 \le C+C\sum_{\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^k}(1+|\mathbf n|)^2e^{-2\beta|\mathbf n|}
 <\infty.
\]
Every term in the generator therefore maps $\sqrt\sigma$ into
Hilbert--Schmidt space, and invariance
gives $L\sqrt\sigma=0$ in this coefficient formula.  Thus the closed
form on $D(\mathcal K^{1/2})$ also annihilates $\sqrt\sigma$.
For $\mathsf P_J=\mathbf1_{[0,J]}(\mathcal K)$, this gives
\[
 \|(\mathcal K+I)^{1/2}(I-\mathsf P_J)\sqrt\sigma\|_2\longrightarrow0,
\]
so adding $\sqrt\sigma$ does not change the closed form.  This proves that
$\mathscr F$ is a form core for the constructed operator $L$;
the coefficient formula also gives $\mathscr F\subset D(L)$.
The parameters in \cref{lem:oscillator-smoothing} can now be chosen as
\[
 \theta_*=\beta/4,\qquad
 \kappa_*=v\bigl(\cosh\beta-\cosh(\beta/2)\bigr)>0,
 \qquad s_*=\frac{\beta}{2\kappa_*},
\]
because $c/v=\cosh\beta$.  The lemma gives
\eqref{eq:oscillator-smoothing}.

\emph{Step 3: the endpoint and entropy decay.}
The operator
$B_*=\sigma^{-1/8}e^{-\beta \mathsf N/4}$
has a bounded extension.  Since $H_{0,n}=k+2\mathsf N$,
its two blocks are
\[
 B_*=\Pi_MB_*\Pi_M+Z^{1/8}e^{\beta k/8}(I-\Pi_M).
\]
The first block is a finite matrix and the second is scalar.
For $Y\in D(e^{(\beta/4)\mathcal K})$, first on finite matrices and
then by closure,
\begin{align*}
 \|Y\|_{4\leftarrow2,\sigma}
 &=\|\sigma^{-1/8}Y\sigma^{-1/8}\|_4
 =\|B_*(e^{(\beta/4)\mathcal K}Y)B_*^\dagger\|_4\\
 &\le\|B_*\|_\infty^2\|e^{(\beta/4)\mathcal K}Y\|_4
 \le\|B_*\|_\infty^2\|e^{(\beta/4)\mathcal K}Y\|_2.
\end{align*}
Putting $Y=e^{-s_*L}X$ and using the oscillator estimate gives
\[
 \|e^{-s_*L}X\|_{4\leftarrow2,\sigma}
 \le\|B_*\|_\infty^2e^{C_*s_*}\|X\|_2.
\]
It follows that $\|T_{s_*}:L^2(\sigma)\to L^4(\sigma)\|\le C$,
where $C=\max\{1,\|B_*\|_\infty^2e^{C_*s_*}\}<\infty$.
The form comparison also proves compactness.  For
$\mathsf P_J=\mathbf1_{[0,J]}(\mathcal K)$ and integer $J\ge0$,
\[
 \|(I-\mathsf P_J)X\|_2^2
 \le\frac{\|(\mathcal K+I)^{1/2}X\|_2^2}{J+1}
 \le\frac{\mathcal E(X)+c_2\|X\|_2^2}{c_1(J+1)}.
\]
Since $\mathsf P_J$ has finite rank, the form unit ball is relatively
compact in Hilbert--Schmidt space.  This is the compact embedding
criterion for compact resolvent
\cite[Sections~10.3 and 12.1]{Schmdgen2012}.
The nonvanishing-filter kernel argument for finite-rank perturbations
in \cite[Section~3.3]{BeckerRouzeSalzmannCoulomb2026} gives
$\ker L=\mathbb C\sqrt\sigma$.  Hence $\lambda=\operatorname{gap}(L)>0$.
By \cref{lem:gap-strictification}, one may take
\[
 s_{n,M}=s_*+\frac{\log C+\frac12\log3}{\lambda}.
\]
Finally \cref{thm:KMS-endpoint} gives the stated entropy estimate,
for example with
$\alpha_{n,M}=(2s_*+(2\log C+1)/\lambda)^{-1}>0$.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:holding-obstruction}
Let $T_t$ be a conservative continuous-time Markov semigroup on a countable
set $\Omega$ with faithful invariant probability $\pi$.  For distinct $x,y\in\Omega$, let $q(x,y)\ge0$ be the transition rate
from $x$ to $y$, and put $q(x)=\sum_{y\ne x}q(x,y)$, the total rate
out of $x$.  Here $L^p(\pi)$ has norm
$\|f\|_{p,\pi}=(\sum_{x\in\Omega}\pi(x)|f(x)|^p)^{1/p}$.  If there are points $x_k$ such
that
\[
 \pi(x_k)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad \sup_k q(x_k)\le\Lambda<\infty,
\]
then for every $p>2$ and every finite $t>0$,
\[
 \|T_t:L^2(\pi)\to L^p(\pi)\|=\infty.
\]

Let $\mathbf1_{\{x_k\}}$ be the indicator of the singleton $\{x_k\}$
and set $f_k=\pi(x_k)^{-1/2}\mathbf1_{\{x_k\}}$, so
$\|f_k\|_{2,\pi}=1$.  The event that the chain makes no jump before time
$t$ has probability at least $e^{-\Lambda t}$ when it starts from
$x_k$.  Hence
\[
 (T_tf_k)(x_k)\ge e^{-\Lambda t}\pi(x_k)^{-1/2}
\]
and therefore $\|T_tf_k\|_{p,\pi}
 \ge e^{-\Lambda t}\pi(x_k)^{1/p-1/2}\longrightarrow\infty.$
